evidence.title: An LLM chatbot to facilitate primary-to-specialist care transitions: a randomized controlled trial
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated referral quality: co-designed model vs same model fine-tuned on local dialogues
evidence.effect: Fine-tuning on local dialogues lowered quality: history-taking 4.56 vs 3.86, diagnosis 4.67 vs 2.47, test ordering 4.23 vs 2.21 (all P < 0.001); data-tuned model failed to provide diagnoses in 30.0% and tests in 39.3%.
evidence.quote: The co-designed model achieved significantly higher-quality rating scores than the data-tuned counterpart (the co-designed model further fine-tuned on the primary care dialogues) group across all domains: history-taking (without data-tuned 4.56 ± 0.65 versus data-tuned 3.86 ± 0.81; P < 0.001; Fig. 4b ), diagnosis (without data-tuned 4.67 ± 0.55 versus data-tuned 2.47 ± 1.44; P < 0.001) and testing order (without data-tuned 4.23 ± 1.09 versus data-tuned 2.21 ± 1.12; P < 0.001).

evidence.title: Scalable federated learning for emergency care using low cost microcomputing: Real-world, privacy preserving development and evaluation of a COVID-19 screening test in UK hospitals
evidence.outcome: Effect of site-personalisation (local tuning) of the global model on performance
evidence.effect: Site-personalisation gave no significant overall improvement (AUROC improvement <0.01), which the authors read as high generalisability of the global model.
evidence.quote: Site-personalisation of the global model did not give a significant improvement in overall performance (AUROC improvement <0.01), suggesting high generalisability.
evidence.sample_unit: patients (federated training); 32,986 admissions in prospective evaluation

evidence.title: Multicenter validation study for automated left ventricular ejection fraction assessment using a handheld ultrasound with artificial intelligence
evidence.outcome: Effect of retuning the model with more data on underestimation of larger LV volumes
evidence.effect: Original version underestimated LV volumes for larger LV (overall EDV bias 42.1 mL); newer version tuned with more data on larger LVs mitigated these trends, with similar correlations (ICC > 0.85).
evidence.quote: These trends were mitigated with a newer version of the software tuned using increased data involving larger LVs, showing similar correlations (ICC > 0.85).

evidence.title: Development and Clinical Validation of an Artificial Intelligence-Based Automated Visual Acuity Testing System
evidence.outcome: Speech recognition word error rate before vs after fine-tuning on local Singaporean English data
evidence.effect: Word error rate fell from 17.83% to 9.81% for letters and from 2.76% to 1.97% for numbers after fine-tuning on local data.
evidence.quote: The fine-tuned model reduced word error rates from 17.83% to 9.81% for letters and 2.76% to 1.97% for numbers.

evidence.title: Research on the generalization of a blood donor recruitment framework based on machine learning
evidence.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
evidence.outcome: Recall at new sites after fine-tuning with 10% local data
evidence.effect: Fine-tuning with 10% local data raised Suzhou RF recall from 0.67 to 0.77 and Yangzhou MLP recall from 0.58 to 0.68.
evidence.quote: Subsequent fine-tuning with 10% local data further enhanced performance on top of direct generalization (Suzhou RF recall increased to 0.77, Yangzhou MLP to 0.68), rather than compensating for any shortcomings of generalization.
evidence.sample_unit: prospective SMS recruitment rounds (model development used 11,616 Nanjing SMS records)

evidence.title: ArcMAP - ML assisted medical concept mapping to accelerate NHS data standardization
evidence.outcome: Top-1 accuracy for lab test mapping before vs after fine-tuning on local data
evidence.effect: BioLORD top-1 accuracy rose from 37.0% (baseline) to 91.6% after fine-tuning on local hospital data; all models reached 89.0-93.0% top-1 with full training data.
evidence.quote: Our results demonstrate the importance of domain-specific fine-tuning, with top-1 accuracy for laboratory test names increasing from 37.0% to 91.6%.
evidence.sample_unit: source concepts (6,179 medication names and 2,261 laboratory test names)

evidence.title: Multicenter External Validation of the PIPRA Model for Postoperative Delirium in Older Adults
evidence.outcome: Need for local recalibration given imperfect calibration in external validation
evidence.effect: Imperfect calibration, particularly at higher risks, limits direct use of absolute risk estimates; local recalibration required before implementation.
evidence.quote: Local recalibration and dedicated implementation studies are required before considering its general implementation to guide targeted delirium prevention.

evidence.title: Clinical Validation of AI/ML Based Model for Down Syndrome Detection Through Graphical Analysis of Facial Dysmorphic Features
evidence.outcome: Effect of adjusting confidence threshold on Down Syndrome detection sensitivity
evidence.effect: Adjusting the confidence threshold gave 100% sensitivity at the cost of more false positives; default threshold 0.5 gave precision 86.67%, recall 92.86%.
evidence.quote: On adjustment of software parameters (the confidence threshold of prediction), the technique can deliver highly accurate Down Syndrome diagnosis with a 100% Sensitivity, at the expense of false positives that may be ruled out through further confirmatory testing.

evidence.title: Managing AI-Enabled Uncertainty in Clinical AI Deployment: Mixed-Methods Study of Governance, Workflow, and Organizational Learning in an ICU Decision Support Pilot
evidence.outcome: Change in CDSS mean absolute error for ICU length-of-stay after model update
evidence.effect: CDSS mean absolute error decreased from 5.95 to 4.12 days after the first model update (exploratory refinement; no comparator).
evidence.quote: Live benchmarking functioned as a feedback loop and supported exploratory model refinement, with CDSS mean absolute error decreasing from 5.95 to 4.12 days after the first model update.

evidence.title: Health system-scale language models are all-purpose prediction engines
evidence.outcome: Generalizability of language model to different sites after site-specific fine-tuning
evidence.effect: Fine-tuning showed potential for increasing generalizability to different sites; no numeric results given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: We additionally demonstrate the benefits of pretraining with clinical text, the potential for increasing generalizability to different sites through fine-tuning and the full deployment of our system in a prospective, single-arm trial.

evidence.title: The Vienna Prediction Model for identifying patients at low risk of recurrent venous thromboembolism: a prospective cohort study
evidence.outcome: O/E ratio after post-hoc recalibration of baseline hazard on cohort data
evidence.effect: Recalibration improved the O/E ratio from 1.6 to 1.03 (95% CI 0.55–1.74) on internal bootstrap validation. External validation of the recalibrated model is still needed.
evidence.quote: Internal bootstrap validation of this recalibration step indicated an O/E ratio of 1.03 (95% CI 0.55–1.74) of the updated VPM.

evidence.title: Optimizing efficiency of a custom clinical decision support tool improves adult congenital heart disease care
evidence.venue: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
evidence.outcome: Proportion of alerts correctly identifying eligible ACHD patients
evidence.effect: Following local diagnostic-code refinements and addition of department encounter criteria, median true-positive alerts increased from 47.3 % to 78.9 %.
evidence.quote: Following the changes implemented in August 2021, there was a significant increase in true positive CDS, which has sustained, and the median of percent true positives increased to 78.9 %, an improvement from the baseline median of 47.3 %.

evidence.title: The incremental design of a machine learning framework for medical records processing
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Document classification accuracy after retraining on data from newly onboarded clinics
evidence.effect: Retraining document classification increased accuracy by 10.2%; performance decline from expansion mitigated through retraining
evidence.quote: Retraining document classification increased accuracy by 10.2%.

evidence.title: Prompt engineering on leveraging large language models in generating response to InBasket messages
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: patient preference for AI response
evidence.effect: Patient preference for tone and quality increased from <15% to 62% with local prompt tuning.
evidence.quote: When comparing responses created from the final prompt to the initial prompt, patient preference shifted to the optimized prompt (V3) based LLM-generated responses for tone ( Figure 4B , N = 154, 62%) and quality ( Figure 4B , N = 154, 62%), significantly higher than preference to the first iteration of prompt based LLM-generated response (<15% for both tone or overall quality) with P -value less than .001.

evidence.title: Behind the Curtain: Comparing Predictive Models Performance in 2 Publicly Insured Populations
evidence.outcome: Predictive performance of population-adapted vs unadapted model in Medicaid
evidence.effect: Model trained on each population performed well in both; applying Medicare coefficients to Medicaid (unadapted) showed poor performance relative to the adapted model.
evidence.quote: The unadapted Medicaid model displayed poor performance relative to the adapted model.

evidence.title: Developing and validation of a smartphone app for post-discharge early follow-up after colorectal cancer surgeries
evidence.outcome: Complication detection across successive algorithm adjustment phases after interim analyses
evidence.effect: Ability to detect complications increased with each adjustment phase; final phase sensitivity 75%, specificity 83%, accuracy 82%, PPV 27%, NPV 97%.
evidence.quote: The ability to detect complications increased with each adjustment phase, and after the third and last phase, the digital solution identified 3(4.8%) real complications, with a sensitivity of 75%, specificity of 83%, accuracy of 82%, positive predictive value of 27%, and negative predictive value of 97%.

evidence.title: Development, deployment, and continuous monitoring of a machine learning model to predict respiratory failure in critically ill patients
evidence.outcome: External-site AUC before and after fine-tuning on local data
evidence.effect: Fine-tuning on MIMIC-IV data raised AUC from 0.73 to 0.873. Acceptable performance was reached using 25% or more of the local training data.
evidence.quote: The fine-tuned Vent.io model achieved an AUC of 0.873.
evidence.sample_unit: ICU encounters (26,045 development, 276 prospective silent-mode, 35,534 MIMIC-IV)

evidence.title: Evolution of an Artificial Intelligence-Powered Application for Mammography
evidence.outcome: Performance after model adjustments
evidence.effect: Following model adjustments based on local testing, the AUC improved by 24.7% (from 0.73 to 0.91) and accuracy by 15.6%.
evidence.quote: Specifically, the AUC rose by 24.7% (from 0.73 to 0.91), the accuracy improved by 15.6% (from 0.77 to 0.89), sensitivity grew by 37.1% (from 0.62 to 0.85), and specificity increased by 10.7% (from 0.84 to 0.93).

evidence.title: Leveraging AI to Drive Timely Improvements in Patient Experience Feedback: Algorithm Validation
evidence.outcome: Theme and sentiment accuracy before vs after local recoding/retraining with trust-specific coded data
evidence.effect: Theme accuracy rose after recoding: Trust A 57% to 76%, B 69% to 78%, C 84% to 90%, D 67% to 82%, GP/community 64% to 77%; sentiment also improved (e.g., A 76% to 82%).
evidence.quote: The accuracy for the theme improved in all the organizations demonstrating that while the algorithm may not initially be transferable, with some retraining and adaptations, it can easily be reused in different service settings.
evidence.sample_unit: NHS trusts (500-comment stratified manually coded sample per trust for accuracy)

evidence.title: National indication protocol for proton radiotherapy in esophageal cancer patients in the Netherlands
evidence.venue: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
evidence.outcome: Performance of externally validated mortality model after local recalibration in esophageal cancer cohorts
evidence.effect: Model performed well after updates to the intercept (both cohorts) and slope (nCRT).
evidence.quote: The model performed well after updates to the intercept (both cohorts) and slope (nCRT).

evidence.title: An Artificial Intelligence Oracle for Proactive Population Health Quality Improvement
evidence.venue: NEJM catalyst innovations in care delivery
evidence.outcome: Actionable true-positive rate of AI safety alerts after iterative prompt refinement
evidence.effect: Actionable true-positive rate improved from 68% of 147 alerts to over 95% of 203 alerts over 12 weeks of clinician-led prompt refinement
evidence.quote: Iterative refinement of the AI prompts, driven by clinical leadership review, improved the actionable true-positive rate of safety alerts from 68% of 147 to over 95% of 203 over 12 weeks.

evidence.title: Large-scale esophageal cancer screening through noncontrast computed tomography and artificial intelligence
evidence.outcome: False positives after calibration on real-world local cohort data
evidence.effect: Calibration in real-world cohort (three centers, n = 35,402) reduced false positives by 72.7% while preserving sensitivity; prospective PPV 42.2%, low-dose screening specificity 99.94%.
evidence.quote: Calibration in a real-world cohort (three centers, n = 35,402) reduced false positives by 72.7% while preserving sensitivity; prospective hospital validation (n = 17,446) achieved a 42.2% PPV, and real-world low-dose screening (n = 10,959) reached 99.94% specificity.

evidence.title: Responsible AI in Action: Planning through Implementation of a Mortality Model for Palliative Care
evidence.outcome: 12-month mortality discrimination (AUC) of locally augmented model versus unmodified commercial model
evidence.effect: Augmenting the commercial EOLCI with local predictors raised AUC from 0.81 (95% CI 0.80, 0.81) to 0.87 (95% CI 0.86, 0.87); SICLI was very well calibrated.
evidence.quote: SICLI was very well calibrated and outperformed the EOLCI (AUC of 0.87 (95% CI:0.86, 0.87) vs. 0.81, (95% CI: (0.80, 0.81)).

evidence.title: External Validation of a Machine Learning Model to Predict Postpartum Hemorrhage in a US Northeastern Healthcare System
evidence.outcome: local refit discrimination and calibration
evidence.effect: Refit model AUC 0.75, but remained poorly calibrated and overestimated PPH risk.
evidence.quote: A refit model achieved improved discrimination (AUC: 0.75) but remained poorly calibrated and overestimated the risk of PPH across a range of predicted probabilities.

evidence.title: Prospective Multicenter Validation of Machine Learning Models for Mortality Prediction in Adult Critically Ill Patients using Transfer Learning
evidence.outcome: Mortality prediction AUC/AUPRC with vs without transfer learning on target-site data
evidence.effect: Domain adaptation improved discrimination across all models (LightGBM AUC p = 0.0010; XGBoost AUPRC p = 0.0419); RF reached 90.7% AUC with DA and 81.3% AUPRC with ITL.
evidence.quote: Results demonstrated that both Domain Adaptation (DA) and Inductive Transfer Learning (ITL) significantly enhanced model performance under realistic conditions where target-domain data are limited.

evidence.title: Development and External Validation of a Treatment-Adjusted Machine Learning Model for Precision Allocation of Group-Based Depression Care Among People Living with HIV in Uganda
evidence.outcome: Calibration (slope, Brier score, AUC) before and after recalibration on external validation set
evidence.effect: Isotonic regression recalibration improved calibration slope from 1.703 to 1.00, Brier score from 0.070 to 0.015, and AUC to 0.986.
evidence.quote: Post-calibration isotonic regression improved probability alignment (slope 1.703 to 1.00; Brier 0.070 to 0.015; AUC 0.986).
evidence.sample_unit: adults living with HIV with depression symptoms (SEEK-GSP trial participants)

evidence.title: Calibration Drift Under Cross-Institutional Deployment: An External Validation Framework for ICU Mortality Prediction Across MIMIC-IV and eICU
evidence.outcome: Expected calibration error after intercept-only recalibration on external data
evidence.effect: An intercept-only adjustment reduced ECE by 26%.
evidence.quote: An intercept-only adjustment reduced ECE by 26%.

evidence.title: A digital twin for hospital antimicrobial resistance forecasting and constrained intervention optimisation
evidence.outcome: Performance when trained in shifted regime versus zero-shot transfer
evidence.effect: Training directly in the shifted regime improved performance compared with zero-shot transfer; portability across regimes can still improve, especially under partial surveillance data.
evidence.quote: When models were trained directly in the shifted regime, performance improved compared with zero-shot transfer, indicating that the digital twin can adapt to new and previously unseen operating conditions but that portability across regimes can improve, particularly when only partial surveillance data are available.

evidence.title: Development and External Validation of a Machine Learning Model for 10-Year Ischemic Stroke Risk Prediction in Diverse Populations
evidence.outcome: Calibration after local intercept recalibration by ancestry group
evidence.effect: BioMe-fit intercept recalibration restored calibration in African American and Hispanic participants but not European American participants.
evidence.quote: Bio  Me -fit intercept recalibration restored calibration in African American and Hispanic but not European American participants.
evidence.sample_unit: patients (34,987 All of Us development cohort; 10,693 BioMe external validation)

evidence.title: Agentic Trial Emulation to Learn Health System-specific Drug Effects At Scale
evidence.outcome: Error between EHR-derived and published log hazard ratios before vs after local Bayesian calibration
evidence.effect: Calibration reduced mean absolute error from 0.567 to 0.224 log-HR (60.5% reduction) in leave-one-out validation; out-of-distribution AVERROES error fell from 0.379 to 0.051 (86.5%).
evidence.quote: In pooled leave-one-out validation, calibration reduced mean absolute error from 0.567 to 0.224 log–hazard ratio (60.5% reduction) and achieved 100% empirical coverage of 95% posterior predictive intervals across held-out trials (4/4).
evidence.sample_unit: trials emulated (three independent agent runs each)

evidence.title: Risk stratification for the rapid pain progression phenotype in knee osteoarthritis using interpretable multimodal machine learning: Development in the Osteoarthritis Initiative and external evaluation in the Prospective Cohort of Osteoarthritis from A Coruña
evidence.outcome: Recalibration of model to correct prevalence shift in external cohort
evidence.effect: Logistic recalibration corrected prevalence shifts; after recalibration the sensitive threshold gave NPV 0.875 and sensitivity 0.804, the high-specificity threshold PPV 0.610 and specificity 0.941.
evidence.quote: Logistic recalibration corrected prevalence shifts.
evidence.sample_unit: individuals in external PROCOAC cohort (1609 instances)

evidence.title: Diagnostic Performance of Fluorescence-Based Rapid On-Site Specimen Evaluation for  Helicobacter pylori  Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing Before and After Algorithm Optimization: A Two-Round Comparative Study
evidence.outcome: Specificity with drug-specific Youden cutoffs vs uniform 50% FRR threshold
evidence.effect: Drug-specific ROC-derived cutoffs improved specificity appreciably compared with the uniform 50% FRR threshold, most evident for levofloxacin hydrochloride.
evidence.quote: ROC analysis showed that drug-specific optimal cutoffs derived from the Youden index improved specificity appreciably compared with the uniform 50% FRR threshold currently applied, the gain being most evident for levofloxacin hydrochloride.

evidence.title: Use of Federated Learning for validating and updating privacy-preserving decentralized multi-study prognostic models in Traumatic Brain Injury
evidence.outcome: Discrimination, calibration and precision of federated-updated versus original IMPACT and single-study models
evidence.effect: Federated models had similar AUC (0.77-0.88) to original and single-study models, were well-calibrated, had higher precision, and reduced the impact of missing data.
evidence.quote: Compared to the original IMPACT and single-study models, both federated models presented similar discrimination (AUC), were well-calibrated, were more efficient (higher precision), and reduced the impact of missing data in model estimation.

evidence.title: Explainable Machine Learning and Temporal Calibration Drift of a TyG- BMI-Based Model for Early Prediction of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus
evidence.outcome: Effect of logistic recalibration on temporal-cohort calibration and Brier score
evidence.effect: Apparent logistic recalibration set intercept to approximately 0 and slope to 1.0 in the temporal cohort and improved XGBoost Brier score from 0.111 to 0.100.
evidence.quote: Apparent logistic recalibration set the intercept to approximately 0 and the slope to 1.0 in the temporal cohort and improved the XGBoost Brier score from 0.111 to 0.100.

evidence.title: Development and External Validation of a Treatment-Adjusted Machine Learning Model to Support Risk-Informed Group-Based Depression Care for People Living with HIV in Uganda
evidence.outcome: Effect of Platt recalibration on external-validation calibration and Brier score of the XGBoost model
evidence.effect: After Platt recalibration, AUC stayed strong (0.940), Brier score improved from 0.174 to 0.113, and calibration slope improved from 7.533 to 1.093.
evidence.quote: Following Platt-recalibration, XGBoost showed the best overall performance, preserving strong discrimination (AUC 0.940) while improving the Brier score from 0.174 to 0.113 and the calibration slope from 7.533 to 1.093.
evidence.sample_unit: adults living with HIV with significant depression symptoms

evidence.title: Silent calibration drift in a frozen clinical prediction model: a decade-long audit and an operational monitoring framework
evidence.outcome: Whether recalibrating with representative contemporaneous data fixes miscalibration
evidence.effect: Contemporaneous intercept recalibration restored calibration-in-the-large (predicted 19.2%→15.6%) without affecting discrimination; stale correction failed to transport.
evidence.quote: Contemporaneous intercept recalibration restored calibration-in-the-large (predicted 19.2%→15.6%) without affecting discrimination; a correction estimated in the earlier era failed to transport and reversed the direction of the bias.

evidence.title: External validation reveals poor calibration despite preserved discrimination for a vasopressin treatment-signal prediction model across ICU databases
evidence.outcome: Calibration slope after local updating (offset-only, recalibration learning curve) in eICU
evidence.effect: Offset-only updating retained a slope of 0.437. At 125 events, same-system median out-of-sample slope was 0.877, but hospital-held-out slope was 0.789 (38.4% within 0.8–1.2).
evidence.quote: Offset-only updating retained a slope of 0.437.
evidence.sample_unit: ICU stays (3,692 training, 1,582 MIMIC-IV internal test, 1,801 eICU-CRD external)

evidence.title: Applying models of care for total hip and knee arthroplasty: External validation of a published predictive model to identify extended stay risk prior to lower-limb arthroplasty
evidence.outcome: performance after local adjustment
evidence.effect: Adjustment improved performance, but calibration remained poor at low and medium risk thresholds; net benefit was modest.
evidence.quote: Performance improved following adjustment of the model intercept and model coefficients, although the model remained poorly calibrated at low and medium risk threshold and net benefit of the adjusted model was modest.

evidence.title: Geographical validation of the Smart Triage Model by age group
evidence.outcome: Neonatal model discrimination after re-estimating intercept, coefficients and thresholds locally
evidence.effect: Neonate AUROC improved from 0.62 to 0.83 (0.79-0.87) with 13% and 41% low- and high-risk thresholds
evidence.quote: After model revision for neonates, we achieved an AUROC of 0.83 (0.79-0.87) with 13% and 41% as the low- and high-risk thresholds, respectively.

evidence.title: Application of MALDI-MS and Machine Learning to Detection of SARS-CoV-2 and non-SARS-CoV-2 Respiratory Infections
evidence.outcome: Local accuracy after retraining ML models on combined South American and Kazakhstan data
evidence.effect: After retraining, SVM-RBF accuracy was 88.0%, 95.0% and 78% for Kazakhstan SARS-CoV-2+, NCARI and AC; SARS-CoV-2 vs. rest ROC AUC 0.983 [0.958, 0.987].
evidence.quote: After re-training of the ML algorithms on the SA-Kaz peak intensity matrix, the accuracy of detection by the top-performing Support Vector Machine with radial basis function kernel model was at 88.0, 95.0 and 78% for the Kazakhstan SARS-CoV-2+, NCARI, and AC subjects, respectively with a SARS-CoV-2 vs. rest ROC AUC of 0.983 [0.958, 0.987]; a high differentiation accuracy was maintained for the South American SARS-CoV-2 and NCARI.

evidence.title: A type 1 diabetes prediction model has utility across multiple screening settings with recalibration
evidence.outcome: Calibration improvement after recalibrating model to local screening cohort
evidence.effect: Brier score improved from 0.40 [0.38,0.43] to 0.16 [0.14,0.17] (p < 0.001) after logistic recalibration in TrialNet
evidence.quote: Adjustment for baseline risk and selection criteria in TrialNet using logistic recalibration improved calibration across all ages (Brier score 0.16 [0.14,0.17]; p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Hazard-aware adaptations bridge the generalization gap in large language models: a nationwide study
evidence.outcome: Generalizability across institutions of adapted prompts versus zero-shot prompts for smoking history extraction
evidence.effect: Adapted prompts, engineered to address observed errors, achieved better generalizability across institutions than zero-shot prompts; macro-F1 0.86 in VA, 0.85 in MIMIC.
evidence.quote: We demonstrate that adapted prompts, engineered to address observed errors, achieve better generalizability across institutions compared to zero-shot prompts.

evidence.title: External validation and update of the J-ACCESS model in an Italian cohort of patients undergoing stress myocardial perfusion imaging
evidence.venue: Journal of nuclear cardiology : official publication of the American Society of Nuclear Cardiology
evidence.outcome: Calibration and discrimination before vs after local recalibration of J-ACCESS model
evidence.effect: Recalibration lowered residual deviance 2090 to 1962 and d mean 0.034 to 0.005; C-statistic 0.664 to 0.666; Brier 0.075 to 0.073; Hosmer-Lemeshow P=.45 after logistic recalibration.
evidence.quote: The recalibrations improved the performance of the initial model.

evidence.title: A recalibrated prediction model can identify level-1 trauma patients at risk of nosocomial pneumonia
evidence.venue: Archives of orthopaedic and trauma surgery
evidence.outcome: Calibration and discrimination after local intercept and full recalibration of imported model
evidence.effect: Intercept moved from -3.08 to 0.80, giving better calibration; full recalibration AUC 0.84 and Brier 0.089 to 0.087; adding age raised AUC to 0.87.
evidence.quote: After intercept recalibration, the model’s intercept increased from -3.08 in the Croce model to 0.80 in our cohort, showing better calibration (Fig. 2 B).

evidence.title: Validation in Indonesia of two published scores for mortality prediction after cardiac surgery
evidence.outcome: Calibration and discrimination after local recalibration of EuroSCORE II
evidence.effect: After recalibration, calibration good (HL P=0.79) and predicted mortality 3.2% vs observed 3.8%; AUC 0.777 not significantly different from original (P=0.92)
evidence.quote: The total mortality rate was slightly underestimated by the recalibrated EuroSCORE II model (3.2% vs. observed mortality 3.8%). However, calibration was still good (HL test P = 0.79, [ Figure 2 ]).

evidence.title: Optimizing the Implementation of Clinical Predictive Models to Minimize National Costs: Sepsis Case Study
evidence.outcome: Cost savings from tuning classification thresholds by diagnostic category for out-of-the-box models
evidence.effect: Heterogeneous thresholds gave gains highest for lower-accuracy models: US $3.7B vs US $3B with uniform at AUC 0.82; overall savings up to 12.3% from customized thresholds.
evidence.quote: Figure 4 C shows that the gains from choosing heterogenous thresholds by MDCs are the highest for lower-accuracy models.

evidence.title: Computed tomography and radiation dose images-based deep-learning model for predicting radiation pneumonitis in lung cancer patients after radiation therapy
evidence.venue: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
evidence.outcome: AUC on external cohorts before and after adjusting model weights with local subset
evidence.effect: Baseline AUC 0.55 (test-set-2) and 0.63 (test-set-3); after adjusting weights with 40 local patients, AUC improved to 0.65 and 0.70.

evidence.effect: Greifswald-modified RetCAD sensitivity for more-than-mild DR 93.63% vs 70.41% unmodified (diagnosable); specificity fell to 66.5%; missed severe DR 2 vs 13, moderate 13 vs 67. Threshold derived and evaluated on the same local data.
evidence.quote: Under this scenario, 2 severe DR cases and 13 moderate DR cases would be missed compared to 13 severe DR and 67 moderate DR cases with unmodified RetCAD screening.

evidence.title: Evaluating the impact of data biases on algorithmic fairness and clinical utility of machine learning models for prolonged opioid use prediction
evidence.outcome: AUROC after retraining model on local VHA data versus external validation
evidence.effect: Retraining increased AUROC in the target cohort from 0.70 to 0.82 (0.12 shift), improving most subgroups, though opioid-exposed disparities persisted.
evidence.quote: In Stage 3, retraining the model increased AUROC in the target cohort from 0.70 to 0.82 (0.12 shift).

evidence.title: Deep learning based semi-automated model can predict lineage in patients with pituitary neuroendocrine tumors
evidence.outcome: External-cohort accuracy after raising the confidence threshold
evidence.effect: Raising the cut-off from 0.8 to 0.9 improved accuracy from 86.0% to 95.1%, comparable to manual evaluation (p=0.293). Workload reduction fell to 39.3%.
evidence.quote: Under this scenario, although the workload reduction was only 39.3%, the accuracy significantly improved to 95.1%.

evidence.title: Domain validation of the CRASH prognostic model for predicting 14-day mortality among patients and traumatic brain injury and intracranial hemorrhage in a Thai emergency department
evidence.outcome: Effect of logistic recalibration of intercept and slope on calibration in local population
evidence.effect: Recalibration reduced overestimation in high-risk groups and better aligned predictions with observed mortality (shown in plots; no numeric post-recalibration metrics in text).
evidence.quote: The recalibration process effectively reduced this overestimation, aligning predicted outcomes with observed mortality rates.

evidence.title: Testing the Transportability of the Psychosis Metabolic Risk Calculator in Canada (Quebec): International External Validation Study
evidence.outcome: Change in performance after updating race/ethnicity predictor using local data
evidence.effect: Full model C=0.74 (0.71-0.77), intercept 0.000, slope 1.001; partial model C=0.71, intercept 0.001, slope 1.005; slight improvement.
evidence.quote: After updating the model with a race and ethnicity predictor calibrated to locally representative categories, performance improved slightly (full model C = 0.74, 95% CI, 0.71-0.77; intercept = 0.000; slope = 1.001; partial model C = 0.71, 95% CI, 0.68-0.74; intercept = 0.001; slope = 1.005).

evidence.title: Deploying machine learning models in clinical settings: a real-world feasibility analysis for a model identifying adult-onset type 1 diabetes initially classified as type 2
evidence.outcome: Performance of locally retrained model versus national model on regional HIE data (AUROC, precision at 5% recall)
evidence.effect: Localized model AUROC 0.774 vs national 0.751; precision at 5% recall 35.4% vs 25.5%; PR CIs overlap, so differences modest and localization is effort-intensive.
evidence.quote: Model localization involved retraining on the regional dataset and resulted in improved AUROC (increased from 0.751 to 0.774), AUPRC (from 5.48% to 6.88%), and precision on the highest scoring patients (from 25.5% to 35.4% at 5% recall).
evidence.sample_unit: adult type 2 diabetes patients in regional HIE dataset (2,564,877 patient cross-sections)

evidence.title: Recalibration of the Framingham coronary heart disease risk score for a selected Sri Lankan population and its association with carotid artery intima-media thickness: A cross-sectional study
evidence.outcome: Association of original vs locally recalibrated Framingham risk categories with carotid IMT
evidence.effect: Recalibrated models gave lower overall CHD risk estimates than the original score and showed stronger CIMT associations; CIMT differed by risk category (P<.05), with higher CIMT values in rFRS models.
evidence.quote: The recalibrated FRS models provided lower overall CHD risk estimates while maintaining stronger associations with CIMT than the original FRS, supporting their improved applicability for CHD risk prediction in the Sri Lankan population.

evidence.title: Real world deployment of a pancreatic cancer risk model: impact of refitting, imputation, and computational burden
evidence.outcome: Discrimination and calibration before versus after refitting model on recent local data
evidence.effect: Refitting improved C-index across all scenarios (e.g., non-imputed 0.69 to 0.81) and improved alignment of predicted and observed risk.

evidence.title: Bridging the analog divide: a comparison of printed X-ray films and digital images when using computer-aided detection software for tuberculosis screening
evidence.outcome: Specificity after choosing tuned abnormality score thresholds to reach target sensitivity
evidence.effect: Calibrating thresholds to 90% sensitivity gave specificity of 89.3% (DICOM) and 81.1% (JPEG), meeting the TPP criteria.
evidence.quote: When the software's abnormality score thresholds were calibrated to achieve 90% sensitivity, Genki maintained high specificity with both DICOM (89.3%) and JPEG (81.1%) file types, meeting the minimum Target Product Profile (TPP) criteria for a high-sensitivity, high-specificity screening test.

evidence.title: Foundation models enable wearable signal screening for cardiovascular disease among people living with HIV
evidence.outcome: CVD detection AUROC with vs without locally trained classifier on foundation model embeddings
evidence.effect: Zero-shot NormWear PPG AUROC 0.560 (AP 0.226); NormWear with local classifier 0.667; frozen PaPaGei plus locally trained calibrated classifier AUROC 0.769 (AP 0.489). Small sample (13 cases), confounded by model differences.
evidence.quote: Our zero-shot baseline (NormWear, AUROC 0.560) represents truly label-free deployment but yields insufficient discrimination, highlighting that some local labels substantially improve utility.

evidence.title: External validation and logistic recalibration of POSSUM and P-POSSUM for predicting postoperative morbidity and mortality after elective hepatic resection
evidence.outcome: Calibration of POSSUM/P-POSSUM before and after local logistic recalibration
evidence.effect: Original models underestimated events; bootstrap-corrected recalibration gave slopes 0.837-0.907 and intercepts 0.16 to -0.34, improving calibration without materially changing AUC.
evidence.quote: Our findings support the notion that logistic recalibration can reduce systematic calibration errors without materially changing discrimination [ 13 , 25 ].

evidence.title: How threshold customisation affects the performance of a multiclass X-ray AI model for primary care triage: a retrospective study
evidence.outcome: Local threshold tuning versus vendor default on representative polyclinic data
evidence.effect: Default 0.15 gave sensitivity 87.3%, NPV 87.0%; tuned 0.10 gave sensitivity 93.2%, NPV 91.3%, specificity 71.7%.
evidence.quote: We found that the threshold required for optimal performance of Lunit CXR as a co-triage tool was different from the default threshold of 0.15 set by Lunit.

evidence.title: External validation of the PREVENT risk score: performance and clinical utility in an Iranian population
evidence.outcome: Effect of local recalibration-in-the-large on predicted risk, sensitivity, and net benefit
evidence.effect: Recalibration raised mean predicted risk in men from 4.2% to 7.6%, sensitivity from 62.4% to 79.9% at 5% threshold; net benefit rose modestly (0.0356 to 0.040 in men); NRI +61% men, +79% women.
evidence.quote: Calibration-in-the-large improved model performance in both sexes, most notably in men, increasing mean predicted risks to 7.6% in men and 4.3% in women.

evidence.title: Weakly supervised deep learning for cutaneous squamous and basal cell carcinoma in whole-slide histopathology

evidence.title: An artificial intelligence prediction model for optimizing patient selection for cardiac imaging for the investigation of suspected coronary artery disease

evidence.quote: Following updating, model AUROC recovered almost entirely at 0.794 (95% CI: 0.794, 0.795) compared with 0.807 (95% CI: 0.806, 0.808) for the original local test set.

evidence.title: Multicenter validation and updating of the ELDER-ICU model for severity assessment in elderly critical illness

evidence.quote: However, retraining markedly outperformed incremental training in Asia, achieving larger AUROC gains in both South Korea (ΔAUROC: +0.066) and China (ΔAUROC: +0.076).

evidence.title: Performance of PREVENT Cardiovascular Risk in Electronic Health Record-Based Clinical Practice

evidence.title: External Validation and Recalibration of a Risk Calculator for Major Bleeding After Diagnostic Kidney Biopsy
evidence.outcome: Model performance after recalibration in combined cohort versus original model
evidence.effect: Recalibration improved performance: C-statistic 0.84 (95% CI 0.79-0.89), calibration slope 0.82 (0.75-0.89), intercept -0.49; original external slope 0.72.
evidence.quote: Model performance improved with recalibration in the combined dataset; the estimated C-statistic was 0.84 (95% CI, 0.79-0.89), calibration slope 0.82 (95% CI, 0.75-0.89) and calibration intercept −0.49 (95% CI, −0.7 to −0.25).

evidence.title: A TyG-UHR-based machine learning model for screening lean MAFLD: development and external validation
evidence.outcome: Calibration/probability accuracy on external NHANES hold-out before vs after local recalibration
evidence.effect: Brier score fell from 0.286 to 0.109 and log loss from 1.253 to 0.388 after recalibration; AUC 0.826 vs 0.810; calibration intercept 0.103, slope 0.684.
evidence.quote: Probability accuracy improved significantly: the Brier score decreased from 0.286 to 0.109, and the log loss from 1.253 to 0.388.

evidence.title: Multi-source data integration through pooling and transfer learning improves generalizability and specialization of deep learning models for ICU mortality and length of stay prediction: a four-database external validation study
evidence.outcome: Performance of local tuning strategies (transfer learning, pooling) versus single-source models on target databases
evidence.effect: Data pooling and transfer learning improved specialization; pooling matched or outperformed transfer learning, e.g. RLoS MAPE 84.49 vs. 89.24; Mcomposite improved up to 8.0% over single-source models.
evidence.quote: Data pooling emerged as the superior strategy, achieving the best generalization (Mcomposite improvement up to 8.0% over single-source models) while matching or outperforming transfer learning for specialization - particularly for RLoS (MAPE 84.49 vs. 89.24, non-overlapping confidence intervals).

evidence.title: Predicting Treatment Response After Total Neoadjuvant Therapy for Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer
evidence.outcome: Brier score in external cohort before and after local recalibration
evidence.effect: External validation Brier score 0.30 (95% CI 0.26-0.33), improving to 0.17 with recalibration.
evidence.quote: At external validation in a cohort of 83 patients that are being managed with TNT+W/W (median age 57; 37% female), the model predicted pcCR with an AUROC 0.69 (95% CI 0.57-0.82), AUPRC 0.90 (95% CI 0.82-0.96), and Brier score of 0.30 (95% CI 0.26-0.33), improving to 0.17 with recalibration.

evidence.title: External validation of machine learning models for estimation of mortality 1, 3, 6, and 12 months after hip fracture on 5,055 consecutive patients

evidence.effect: Average predicted 12-month risk 0.38 vs observed 0.27 before recalibration; 0.24 after. Predicted risks after recalibration were 0.07, 0.12, 0.17, 0.24 vs observed 0.08, 0.15, 0.20, 0.27. AUC unchanged.
evidence.quote: The calibration at large and the flexible calibration curves were initially slightly off but were greatly improved by recalibration with bootstrapped isotonic regression.

evidence.title: Performance of multivariable risk prediction algorithms in predicting COPD exacerbations: a population-based study

evidence.quote: Recalibration resolved this overprediction, yielding O/E ratio of 1.00 (95% CI 0.99 to 1.00), while maintaining discrimination (AUC: 0.77).

evidence.title: The Role of AI-Based Software BrainScan in the Interpretation of Non-Contrast Head CT in Acute Ischemic Stroke: An External Validation Study
evidence.outcome: Ischemia sensitivity after threshold recalibration to Youden-optimal cutoff
evidence.effect: Default threshold sensitivity 59.2%; Youden-optimal threshold (0.055) recovered sensitivity to 86.1% with negligible specificity loss
evidence.quote: The Youden-optimal threshold (0.055) recovered sensitivity to 86.1% with negligible specificity loss, reflecting a markedly bimodal score distribution.

evidence.title: Validating predictive models on EHRs data : lessons learnt from the NCDR-IMPACT-score applied on a French cardiac catheterization cohort

evidence.effect: Local recalibration improved AUC from 0.642 (original IMPACT-score) to 0.719 (IMPACT-score-Necker); original AUC was 0.752 in NCDR-IMPACT validation cohort.

evidence.title: Benchmarking of radiobiological NTCP models in head and neck radiotherapy using independent computational pipelines: an institutional validation study with machine learning augmentation

evidence.title: Evaluating the Google CT Foundation model for central pulmonary embolism detection on computed tomography pulmonary angiograms

evidence.title: Large language model driven multicenter prediction and explainable risk attribution of acute kidney injury

evidence.title: Leveraging ECG foundation models in critical care for sinus rhythm and atrial fibrillation classification

evidence.title: Assessing generalizability of an AI-based visual test for cervical cancer screening

commentary.bottom_line: Studies of local tuning mostly report better accuracy, recall, or calibration on local data, but the one randomized trial found that fine-tuning a model on local dialogues lowered referral quality. Health systems may plan for local tuning while treating each retuned model as a new version that must be tested against the original before clinical use.

perspectives.view: Of 207 studies testing local tuning, the one randomized trial found that fine-tuning on local dialogues lowered referral quality. Most prospective comparisons report gains in accuracy, recall, or calibration, and one federated study found AUROC gains under 0.01. Outcomes are technical, many designs lack comparators, and interventions vary, so certainty is low.

Tuning can introduce new errors. In the trial, the locally tuned model failed to provide diagnoses in 30.0% of cases. Elsewhere, calibration on local data cut false positives by 72.7% while preserving sensitivity, and a threshold change raised sensitivity to 100% at the cost of more false positives. These results suggest retuned models need retesting before release.

Some studies suggest modest local data can suffice. Fine-tuning with 10% of local data raised recall from 0.67 to 0.77 at one site, and 25% or more of local data gave acceptable ICU performance. Fundus AUC reached 0.82 at about 500 images, with smaller gains beyond that. Clinician-led prompt refinement ran over 12 weeks.

The only trial, in rural, low-income, low-literacy Chinese populations, found that local fine-tuning lowered quality. In Medicaid, a population-adapted model outperformed Medicare coefficients applied unchanged, and prompt refinement raised actionable alerts above 95%. Rural sites in the United States failed sample size requirements for local recalibration, which may leave small sites unable to tune.

Retraining after onboarding new clinics raised document classification accuracy by 10.2%, and mammography AUC rose from 0.73 to 0.91 after adjustments based on local testing. Adding local predictors to a commercial model raised AUC from 0.81 to 0.87 offline. Budgets may need to cover local labeling, retraining, and repeat validation for each update.

Patient preference for the tone and quality of AI message replies rose from under 15% to 62% after local prompt tuning. In the trial of patient-facing referral dialogues, the locally tuned model lowered history-taking, diagnosis, and test-ordering scores. Patients may benefit from tuning only when each retuned tool is checked against its prior version.

commentary.research_gap: No study linked local tuning to patient outcomes such as missed diagnoses or alarm burden, and few compared tuned and untuned models concurrently in the same population. Controlled studies are needed that define minimum local sample sizes, test retuned versions against the originals before release, and report results separately for small and safety-net sites.
commentary.underserved_note: The one randomized trial enrolled limited English proficiency, low-literacy, low-income, and rural patients in China and found that local fine-tuning lowered quality, while two lower-level studies in the United States that included Medicaid populations reported gains. No study tested tuning in safety-net hospitals in the United States serving limited English proficiency patients, and a rural hazard study suggests small sites may lack enough data to recalibrate at all.
